pr_title: Hide non-interactive elements on multi-spectator players
pr_body:
Closes #14261 

Video to quickly showcase how this looks now:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22781491/129304090-f55d4d4d-55bf-41b5-9818-47ab36772054.mp4
pr_comments: What about the hold to quit button?
We should be removing all the interactive elements that can't be clicked (until they can) I guess?

Yeah seems the "hold to quit" button is the only uninteractive elements which should be hidden, the song progress should remain to point out the current time of the spectator player, but the bar should be hidden like in regular solo mode. Will do that.

Fwiw this wasn't the way I was going to go about this - I was thinking of making `HUDOverlay` derivable instead and a custom `MultiSpectatorPlayerHUDOverlay` or something like that. Because it's a bit haphazard with the way that the "Watching X" text is added to `SpectatorPlayer` itself completely outside of the HUD...

But hiding individual elements seems fine as a stop-gap solution.

Honestly as this is probably a temporary thing, I'd just call `.Expire()` on the elements, keeping all the logic in one place? Not sure.. Potentially not even exposing, but just using `ChildrenOfType` and avoiding making changes to any of the base classes.
Expiring does seem to work and simplify logic, have switched to it now.
I've made some changes to avoid exposing a new bindable from `Player`. Would appreciate a double-check review from someone else.

comments: The spectator interface is still very raw, but if this can be done with minimal effort then it's probably a good quick improvement.

review_comments: This reads a little funny, maybe, but it makes some sense to a degree... I think the biggest throw-off here is `HasReplayLoaded` being bindable. This is really just a set in practice but looks like a strange conditional bind. I don't see how to improve this either, so...
Can agree; was just leaving it how it was on `master`.

???

please check the CI again. this is hiding the test failure rather than correctly testing it. it only failed once out of all the runs. now it's going to silently pass on a wrong condition. i believe you need a wait step as song process is async loaded.

yeah well, the reason I chose `AddUntilStep` was that it may take more than one frame for this check to pass due to certain components not loading at once.

will go with `AddWaitStep` then with explanatory comment
what you had was more correct, it just read wrong to me.
Right... my brain already halted while I was pushing that change. I think `AddUntilStep` *with* an explanatory comment should read well.
This test step is consistently failing for me in test browser/non-headless.
It passes locally for me? can you provide the thrown exception and the stack trace? weird it fails

It just times out after the 50 repeats allowed. No stack trace.

![2021-08-14-190759_232x378_scrot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20418176/129455008-675ce86f-8f35-4ec3-8c79-ec255d035e7b.png)

Hmm, I'm still not sure what the cause of that could be, as I've tried multiple times with different skins and always been passing the test. Would need you to debug this failure in that case, as I can't reproduce.
If anything, I think it will be a client side setting (some kind of HUD toggle or otherwise).

You're right, turns out hiding the HUD overlay blocks `SkinnableTargetContainer` from fininshing async load of components, as it schedules the lambda and never gets invoked until the HUD overlay gets updated.

Appears to be a trivial one to solve, will do and open another PR for that.
In addition to https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/14337, I've forced the HUD visibility mode to "Always" in the test case just to make sense of things.
